title: Ethiopian Roasted Chickpeas
community: All of Ethiopia — the dry-roasted chickpea snack
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Roasted Chickpeas — soaked chickpeas dry-roasted until golden, crunchy, and nutty. Part of the Qolo tradition with barley (ETH018) — eaten at coffee ceremonies, at markets, and throughout fasting periods as the primary protein snack.
longDesc: Roasted chickpeas are the protein backbone of the Ethiopian snack tradition — eaten alongside or mixed with roasted barley (as part of full Qolo), they provide high-quality plant protein in a completely natural, unprocessed snack.
ingredients: // Optional flavourings: berbere or mitmita for spiced version
equipment: Heavy dry pan or oven at 200°C
steps: Drain soaked chickpeas. Rinse. Spread on a cloth and dry completely (minimum 1 hour).
Pan method: heat dry pan over medium heat. Add chickpeas.
Roast stirring constantly 20—25 minutes until golden-brown and crunchy.
Oven method: toss dried chickpeas with ½ tsp oil. Spread on baking sheet. Roast at 200°C 25—30 minutes, shaking halfway.
Season with salt while still hot.
Cool completely before eating — they crisp further.
chefTips: Complete drying before roasting is essential — wet chickpeas steam and become tough.
Cool before tasting — they taste soft when hot but crisp fully as they cool.
The pan method produces more even results than the oven.
cookingScience: See ETH138 for roasted chickpea science. The oven method produces a slightly different result from pan-roasting — the dry oven heat dehydrates more evenly from all sides, while pan-roasting creates direct Maillard contact on one side at a time.
servedWith: Mixed with roasted barley as Qolo (ETH018)
healthBenefits: No added fat in pan-roasted version.
culturalNote: Roasted chickpeas are Ethiopia's most democratic snack — available to everyone, from the highland farmer to the city schoolchild. A handful of roasted chickpeas passed between friends is the simplest expression of Ethiopian social sharing.
